Signature menu items include well-marbled ribeye, sweet-marinated galbi, and thick aged pork belly, along with healthy sides such as yukhoe bibimbap and sprout-and-water-dropwort bibimbap. Professional chefs grill the meat for you, and seasonal house-made sauces, fresh vegetables, and clean side dishes are served together. A value lunch special set is offered at lunchtime (11:00-13:00), and soju/wine pairing sets in the evening. description: Tongui-dong Gukbingwan is a hidden gem near Gyeongbokgung Station where you can enjoy the charm of a hanok in the middle of the city. True to its name, it treats every single guest with the finest service. Here are just three things that set this Seochon favorite apart. First, beef charcoal grilling enjoyed while looking out at the courtyard of a scenic hanok. The interior, using red brick and dark brown wood, brings out a distinctive hanok feel that also makes it a great Gyeongbokgung date course. Sitting comfortably while the beef is pre-grilled in the courtyard is a delightful experience. Briquettes that maintain steady, high heat ideal for grilling beef maximize the smoky flavor. Second, plenty to see. Located near Gyeongbokgung and Gwanghwamun, the surroundings offer many attractions including boutique shops and galleries in Seochon. After a Gyeongbokgung or Blue House tour, our delicious short ribs and Korean dishes will melt away your fatigue. Third, though a grill house, it is also known as a Korean-food destination in Jongno and Gwanghwamun, famous for marinated short ribs cut 3cm thick and aged in a special house sauce, as well as charcoal-grilled deodeok and rich beef-bone tteokguk.

name: Parc
description: Mama knows best! PARC was founded in 2013 in the Hannam district of Seoul, which is the most international neighborhood of Korea's capital city. PARC, which translates to park in the famed romance language of Catalan, serves traditional Korean food inspired from authentic family recipes by owner Pak Mogua's mother, Heo Junghee, that have been passed down through generations of family. After 4 years of traveling the world, Pak realized the strong impact his mother's cooking had always had on him with its unique and genuine flavors. It was then when he decided to collect all of his mother's recipes to not only document for himself, but to also share with people he loved. In the summer of 2012, co-owners Pak Mogua and Oo Zeemin came up with the idea for PARC while sitting in what would eventually become the actual restaurant space. They designed PARC to be casual and affordable, and a friendly restaurant where everyone is welcome and can dine in comfort. PARC prides itself on serving authentic and homemade Korean dishes using the freshest ingredients with both modern and traditional cooking techniques. With a seasonal menu featuring the best of Korean cuisine, we hope you come and try our Korean Mother's Recipes & More. "Parc is my favourite restaurant in Seoul." -Sophie Hicks (Architect, London, UK dined more than 3 times) "This is very warm energy you have here." -Toni Alva (Legenday Skater, CA, USA dined twice)

description: Mokseokjeong is a hidden gem in the quiet alleys of Samcheong-dong, Seoul—a traditional Korean hanok restaurant offering seasonal omakase-style dining. Rather than serving all dishes at once, we present each course in harmony with your pace, always centered around freshly cooked sotbap (Korean pot rice). Our ingredients are handpicked every morning from Garak Market and Majang Meat Market, using only top-grade Hanwoo++ beef and fresh, locally sourced seafood, prepared in limited quantities. This ensures every dish reflects the highest quality and the season’s best flavors. The hanok’s warm, minimalist setting—sunlight filtering through lattice windows, with private rooms for intimate gatherings—creates an ideal space for couples, families, or international guests. Service goes beyond plating; we share the story, seasonal touch, and chef’s intent behind each dish, creating not just a meal but a cherished memory.
